title: Cap. IV Arg. 4: Eph. 1:4 — election in Christ is of believers only; Arminius Exam. Pred. Perk.
pass_a_gloss: Argument 4. Another argument is sought from Eph. 1:4. According as he chose us in him, namely Christ. Whence they argue thus; The election by which God chose us in Christ is only of believers: The election which was made before the foundations of the world were laid was made in Christ: Therefore that is only of believers. The truth of the Major appears from this, that no one can be elected in Christ, except one who is in Christ, of which sort are believers alone. This same argument is urged by Arminius in Exam. Pred. Perk. pages 313, 32, where he has these words, Christ according to the Apostle is not only a means through which salvation already beforehand obtained by election is gotten, but as a meritorious cause, in respect of which election may have been made, and for whom that grace may have been prepared. For God loves no one to eternal life except in Christ: From which it seems to follow, that since no one is considered in Christ by God, unless he be inserted through faith, election is proper to the faithful. These things he.
pass_b_english: Arg. 4. Another argument from Eph. 1:4 — According as he chose us in him, that is Christ. They argue: the election by which God chose us in Christ is of believers only; the election made before the world's foundations was made in Christ; therefore it is of believers only. The Major's truth, they say, is that no one can be elected in Christ unless he is in Christ — and only believers are. Arminius urges the same in Exam. Pred. Perk. pp. 313, 32: on the Apostle, Christ is not only a means through which salvation already gotten by election is obtained, but a meritorious cause in respect of which election is made and for whom that grace is prepared. God loves no one to eternal life except in Christ; so since no one is considered in Christ by God unless inserted by faith, election belongs to the faithful. So he.
source_text: Arg. 4. Aliud argumentum petitur ex Eph. i. 4. Sicut nos elegit in ipso, scil. Christo. Unde sic argumentantur; Electio qua nos elegit in Christo Deus, est tantum credentium: Electio quae facta est ante jacta mundi fundamenta facta est in Christo: Ergo illa credentium tantum est. Majoris veritas ex eo apparet, quod nemo in Christo eligi potest, nisi qui in Christo est, quales sunt soli credentes. Hoc idem argumentum urgitur ab Arminio in Exam. Pred. Perk. pag. 313, 32. ubi haec verba habet, Christus secundum Apostolum, non tantum est medium per quod salus electione jam ante parta obtinetur, sed tanquam causa meritoria, cujus respectu electio facta sit, et propter quem illa gratia sit praeparata. Deus enim neminem ad vitam aeternam amat nisi in Christo: Ex quo sequi videtur, quod cum nemo in Christo consideretur a Deo, nisi ille sit insertus per fidem, Fidelium propria sit electio. Haec ille.
